---
title: "Step 4 — The 9 primers"
subtitle: "Step 4 of 5"
---

**Time:** about 2 hours 45 minutes in total. Do 2 or 3 primers an evening.
**Before you start:** a web browser and an internet connection. Nothing to
install.
**When you finish:** you have written R code and computed a risk ratio, an odds
ratio and a rate.

9 short pages. 5 teach enough R to be useful. 4 teach the epidemiological
arithmetic the lectures assume. Each page has live code cells you edit and run
inside the page itself.

Do them in order. Each page assumes the pages before it.

::: {.callout-important}
## Open these at home, in the week before the course
The first page you open downloads about 17 MB: R itself, compiled to run in a
browser, plus the machinery that marks your answers. Primer 5, which draws
plots, downloads about 37 MB.

Your browser keeps that download for 7 days. Work through these at home this
week and you pay nothing again at IISc.
:::

## How to work through a primer

1. Open the page and wait for the cells to become ready.
2. Press **Run** on every cell, from the top of the page down.
3. Change a number in a cell and press **Run** again.
4. Do each exercise. Press **Hint** before you press **Solution**.

**You should see:** output appearing under each cell after you press Run, and a
green tick when an exercise is correct.

**If it does not work:** see the next section.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this matters
Reading code teaches you very little. The cells exist so that you type, get an
error, and fix it, before Monday rather than during a session.

Reading a solution before you have tried wastes the exercise. The hint exists so
that you do not have to.

Nothing carries from one page to the next. Each page starts R from scratch, so
if you close a page part way through you restart that page, not the sequence.
:::

## If the cells never become ready

Wait 2 or 3 minutes first. The page has to download R before anything runs.

**If it still does not work:**

1. Try a phone hotspot. Institutional and hospital wifi often block this.
2. Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Very old browsers cannot run
   it.
3. For the R primers, work through the [R primer reference](r-primer.qmd) in
   RStudio instead. It teaches the same material.
4. For the epidemiology primers, every answer is printed on the page as ordinary
   text. You can follow those 4 pages with a pencil and a calculator.

There is no Stop button on these pages. If you write a loop that never ends,
reload the page.
